title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Medical Education: An Exploratory Study on the Integration of AI-Supported Personalized Simulation Scenarios
summary: This study explores whether artificial intelligence (AI) can improve training for medical students and healthcare workers. Participants take part in realistic pediatric emergency simulations, during which their stress levels and communication are recorded. After the simulation, some participants receive a debriefing from a human instructor, while others receive a debriefing generated automatically by an AI system. In addition, a written AI-generated feedback report is compared with one written by medical experts. The goal is to find out how helpful, accurate, and supportive AI feedback can be—and whether it can enhance medical learning and preparation for real-life emergencies.
conditions: This study explores the use of AI-based simulations to support healthcare staff in complex decision-making scenarios. The aim is to improve workflow efficiency and to develop preventive strategies that strengthen the ability of clinical staff to manage emergencies safely. In doing so, the study seeks to enhance patient safety while reducing staff workload. The findings will contribute to sustainable solutions for key healthcare challenges such as workforce shortages, increasing workload, and maintaining quality of care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Written informed consent
Medical students from the 6th semester onward from Germany, Austria, and Switzerland
Healthcare professionals from the pediatric department
Compliance with and consent to the technical requirements (e.g., wearable device, audio recording)
Exclusion criteria:
Missing informed consent
Technically unusable data (e.g., corrupted or failed recordings)
Participant withdrawal from the study
